name: Broadcom Inc.

peers.name: Marvell
peers.why: Custom AI chips for Amazon and Microsoft plus data-centre networking and optical chips; same cloud buyers

peers.name: Nvidia
peers.why: The AI-chip leader that Broadcom's custom chips are the alternative to; also competing data-centre Ethernet

peers.name: AMD
peers.why: Rival AI accelerators sold to the same cloud buyers

peers.name: Cisco
peers.why: Own switch chips (Silicon One) compete with Tomahawk/Jericho; enterprise infrastructure software

peers.name: Qualcomm
peers.why: Overlaps in phone radio and wi-fi chips (both sell into Apple)

peers.name: Nutanix
peers.why: Direct rival to VMware in private-cloud software (Broadcom's software side)

valuation.vl3_basis: trailing P/E, 5 years (price / last-12-month SEC diluted EPS, split-adjusted), labelled; GAAP EPS carries VMware intangibles amortisation

dm4.name: AI semiconductor revenue growth vs the prior quarter
dm4.measured_against: the prior quarter (written exception to the year-earlier default, Kenneth 24 Oct 2026, as NVDA DM4a)
dm4.what: How fast Broadcom's AI chip sales (custom AI chips plus AI networking) grew from one quarter to the next.
dm4.why: AI chips are 56% of revenue and nearly all of the growth. At +221% vs a year earlier, year-on-year growth would read strong for quarters after orders peak; quarter-on-quarter growth shows a slowdown two to three quarters sooner.
dm4.bull_means: AI orders are still growing fast quarter to quarter.
dm4.neutral_means: AI growth is slowing to single digits per quarter.
dm4.bear_means: AI chip sales are flat or falling: the sign of a peak.

dm4.name: Infrastructure software (VMware) revenue growth
dm4.what: Growth in Broadcom's software sales, mostly VMware, vs the same quarter last year.
dm4.why: Software is 30% of revenue and the stable, recurring part. VMware price rises after the 2023 purchase are maturing; this shows whether customers keep renewing.
dm4.neutral_means: Software growth is fading to low single digits.
dm4.bear_means: Software is flat or shrinking: customers are leaving VMware.

dm5.name: Big-4 cloud capital spending (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta)
dm5.source: The four companies' quarterly results and SEC filings
dm5.measured_against: same calendar quarter a year earlier
dm5.latest: about +79% (Apr-Jun 2026: $170.1bn vs about $95.0bn); Meta's Sep quarter +80% (21 Oct); the other three report 28-29 Oct
dm5.what: Combined capital spending (data centres and equipment) of the four biggest cloud buyers in the latest quarter vs the same quarter a year earlier.
dm5.why: Google and Meta are Broadcom's largest custom-chip customers; this is their budget, reported by them, and it arrives before Broadcom reports.
dm5.bull_means: Customer budgets are still growing fast.
dm5.bear_means: Budgets are close to flat, which historically comes before chip orders fall.

mix._note: Revenue mix (plan v0.4, not scored). match = regex on the row label printed in the filing; filings from Q1 FY26 print no label for segment revenue, so the engine falls back to the member words (semiconductor solutions / infrastructure software).
mix.note: Broadcom reports revenue and operating profit for its two segments only. AI chips (56% of revenue in Q3 FY26) sit inside Semiconductor solutions and are given only in the results release, not in the SEC filing; the AI split is tracked in DM4a. Segment operating profit excludes unallocated costs (mainly VMware intangibles amortisation and stock pay), so segment margins are higher than the company's reported operating margin.
